bispf-optimized-v2.mechanism_rationale: The first finite regularized Gram solver retained expensive exact-SVD fallbacks on actual convolution gradients. Solver version 2 instead augments the matrix with the original absolute smoothing and applies adaptive finite polar iterations with explicit residual safeguards. This is a distinct numerical recipe and source revision, not an exact trajectory equivalence claim: the converged finite solver omits native hard spectral rank masking. Validate all unchanged public quality gates independently of latency before selecting the whole global recipe. The versioned checkpoint rejects the earlier solver state; no qualification is inherited from bispf-v2 or optimized-v1.

conclusion: Native SVD dominates incumbent BISPF complete-update cost. The first Gram-based Newton–Schulz revision remains slow because actual training gradients trigger exact fallbacks. Augmented solver version 2 removes late r64 fallbacks and lowers its plain median from 605.73 ms to 102.02 ms, but r256 still falls back on approximately 33 critic offsets per late update, retaining a 1513.20 ms plain median. Later solver revisions are separate source/candidate cohorts and receive no evidence transfer from these measurements.
